assumptions: At least one EU importer vertical has recurring difficult-classification events with losses large enough to make external assurance economically plausible, although the packet does not establish which vertical or its case density.
Qualified customs professionals can be contracted to own regulated advice, representation, and escalations on legally workable terms while the founder supplies the workflow and data product.
The 75000 PLN capital estimate can be staged behind paid validation, and the founder remains employed until specialist delivery and account acquisition are shown to fit the stated part-time limit.
evidence_needed_for_higher_score: Paid pilots in one named vertical showing recurring difficult-case volume, quantified avoided losses, annual-contract willingness to pay, renewal intent, repeatable conversion and sales cycle, CAC payback, expert hours and contribution margin, superiority over incumbent alternatives, and explicit permission to reuse de-identified outcomes.

factors.name: Core insight
factors.rationale: The candidate correctly recognizes that free filing, public rulings, and commoditized code prediction move value toward difficult-product fact development, expert-reviewed evidence, monitoring, and exception handling. Direct importer ownership is a coherent refinement, but the insight is not yet tied to a demonstrated underserved vertical.

factors.name: Customer pain and willingness to pay
factors.rationale: Misclassification can affect duties, licences, restrictions, and disputes, so the underlying pain can be consequential. However, no target vertical, loss frequency, case density, price acceptance, or renewal evidence is established, and free official filing plus existing managed services create credible limits on willingness to pay.

factors.name: Business model and economics
factors.rationale: An annual assurance contract plus paid expert escalation could combine recurring revenue with high-value cases, and reusable templates could reduce delivery effort. Pricing, gross margin, expert cost, CAC, payback, retention, case frequency, insurance, support load, owner earnings, and the path to 5 million PLN are all unknown, leaving scalability and profitability weakly substantiated.

factors.name: Market and beachhead
factors.rationale: A single repeat-SKU vertical is appropriately narrow in concept, but no vertical has actually been selected or shown to contain enough reachable importers and recurring difficult cases to form an economically meaningful beachhead.

factors.name: Competitive position and domination potential
factors.rationale: Vertical specialization and direct customer ownership could support a focused position, but Avalara, eClear, TariffPilot, and forwarder-managed services already span automation, APIs, reasoning, human review, and adjacent customs workflows. No exclusive access, proven vertical expertise, or performance advantage supports domination yet.

factors.name: Expansion potential
factors.rationale: A successful vertical workflow could extend to adjacent product categories, EU geographies, rule-change monitoring, disputes, and related compliance tasks. Expansion depends on first proving that templates transfer, experts and regulations can scale, and customers permit reusable learning.

factors.name: Defensibility and durability
factors.rationale: Permissioned product-fact templates, outcome histories, workflow embedding, and direct renewals could compound. Those assets depend on unproven contractual reuse rights and slowly arriving official outcomes, while public EBTI, TARIC, and CLASS information and well-resourced incumbents make the underlying research easy to replicate.

factors.name: Strength of advantage
factors.rationale: The proposed vertical focus and confidential audit trail may improve relevance and trust for difficult cases, but the packet provides no benchmark showing materially better accuracy, speed, risk reduction, price, or user experience than incumbent managed and AI-assisted alternatives.

factors.name: Timing and momentum
factors.rationale: AI can lower workflow-development and research costs while tariff complexity sustains demand for expert judgment. The same technology strengthens incumbents and commoditizes basic classification, and no new regulatory or market catalyst is identified that gives this entrant a temporary opening.

factors.name: Distribution
factors.rationale: Direct account-based outreach avoids dependence on conflicted forwarders and creates ownership of renewal, but reachable account density, conversion, sales cycle, CAC, and referral behavior are unmeasured. Enterprise compliance selling may be slow and socially intensive for a part-time founder, with no established channel advantage.

factors.name: Execution and risks
factors.rationale: The founder's data and automation skills fit the workflow layer, capital is nominally within the stated budget, and expert judgment can in principle be contracted. Execution still requires qualified specialists, insurance, liability allocation, regulatory compliance, accurate product facts, direct sales, and service operations that may conflict with a five-hour daily limit.

highest_value_structural_change: Make the product the vertical system of record for SKU fact intake and classification-change monitoring, with qualified expert review reserved for escalations under a fixed-cost service layer; recurring workflow embedding would reduce dependence on sporadic BTI cases and create clearer switching costs.
main_structural_strength: The design owns the importer renewal relationship and concentrates on a narrow, confidential, expert-backed exception workflow rather than competing as another generic HS-code predictor.
primary_score_limiter: There is no evidence that any specific vertical combines sufficient recurring difficult-case density, annual willingness to pay, affordable acquisition, and scalable expert delivery; that single unproven dependency constrains the market, economics, and repeatability of the model.
strongest_disconfirming_evidence: Polish WIT filing and decisions are free, official tariff and ruling research is broadly public, and multiple incumbents already provide overlapping AI, bulk, API, reasoned-classification, and human-expert services, sharply limiting scarcity and differentiation.
